newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar vols erode into G7 weekend.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols erode into G7 weekend.

text.p: Implied volatilities for short-dated dollar options were weaker in U.S. trading Friday as market participants saw firmness in the spot before the Group of Seven summit as a reason to deflate values.
Currency options traders said the G7 summit this weekend in Denver was keeping market activity to a minimum amid uncertainty over where the dollar was likely headed next.
"Ahead of the G7 people have been very reluctant to do anything," said an options trader for a U.S. bank in New York. "The market is confused as far as the direction of the dollar."

Whether Japan's growing trade surplus becomes a focus at the gathering could determine the dollar's fate, analysts said. U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday expressed concern about persistent trade imbalances in a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Japan's second-quarter tankan survey and May economic indicators will be released next week.
The continued extreme skew to yen calls in risk reversals, at 2.2/2.4, shows fears of further dollar downside have not receded, analysts said.
The dollar was firm at around 114.60 yen while remaining fairly steady against the mark at 1.7275 in the U.S. afternoon.
Dollar/yen volatilities eased substantially in the shorter dates when the spot gained about half a yen overnight, traders in New York said.
"Vols in dollar/yen are just like trading spot. You buy vols if the dollar goes down and sell if it is going up," the U.S. bank trader said.
One-month dollar/yen volatility at midafternoon was 10.8/11.0 percent, having shed roughly 0.8 point from Thursday. One-year was off only slightly at 10.55/10.75 percent.

A New York-based options broker said the sharp drop in volatility presented a buying opportunity and was rekindling interest from the bank sector in buying dollar/yen options, particularly in two- to six-month durations.
He predicted some of the recent volatility sellers would turn buyers on Monday, after sidestepping weekend time decay.
"People are getting a little nervous. Offers are starting to run away," he said.

In dollar/mark, the volatility curve continued to steepen its upward slope. Short-dated values have gradually weakened throughout the week. One-month was 8.4/8.7 percent, down 0.4 point, and one-year was 9.2/9.4 percent, down 0.2 point.
